review.summary: Saffira went first and played the standard turn-one line: discard SDQ to send Prayers and add Saffira, then Manju searched Benten, and Hymn of Light Tributed Benten to summon Saffira, with Benten searching Honest. On turn 2 the player used Ghost Ogre on Blue-Eyes Alternative's effect. It let Saffira be destroyed so Prayers could bring a fresh copy from the Deck, keeping Hymn in the GY. Then Honest beat Titanic Galaxy's attack for 2500 damage. On every later turn Saffira's End Phase effect returned Honest to hand. Honest won a battle on turns 3, 4 and 5, each worth 2500 damage, which took the opponent from 5500 to 0. The SDQ Ritual Summon on turn 3 ran into Spirit Dragon's negation, but the player had expected that and had the Rank 3 fallback ready. No lethal was missed: the most damage available on any turn was 2500. I found no significant mistakes after checking the logged options.

The player went first and played the standard line: discarded SDQ to send Prayers to the GY and add Saffira, Normal Summoned Manju to search Benten, then used Hymn to Ritual Summon Saffira by Tributing Benten, which searched Honest. Over the next turns Saffira, Honest and Saffira's End Phase recursion (Ogre, then Honest twice) won every battle. Each Honest swing dealt 2500 (5500 → 3000 → 500 → 0). Ghost Ogre, Hymn and Sauravis (once from the field, once from the hand) shut down both of Alternative White Dragon's destroy effects. On Turn 5, passing was reasonable: Number 38 can redirect attacks and negate Spells, so no lethal line I could verify existed. The only flaw I found is small: on Turn 3 Sauravis went to Defense when she could safely have attacked Dragon Spirit of White.

mistakes.what: Ritual Summoned Sauravis in face-up Defense, so she couldn't attack that turn.
mistakes.better: In Attack Position, Sauravis (2600 ATK) could have attacked Dragon Spirit of White (2500), the only target that wouldn't run her into the 3000-ATK Blue-Eyes, while Saffira + Honest took care of Blue-Eyes. That deals 100 extra damage and removes a body that later became Xyz material for Number 38. Sauravis would still have been on the field to negate a Special Summon on the opponent's turn.
mistakes.evidence: Defense (2800 DEF) avoids battle damage and is the safer position against their 3000-ATK Blue-Eyes.

review.summary: The player went first and the opponent answered with Maxx "C". On turn 1 it followed the playbook: it discarded SDQ to send Prayers to the GY and add Saffira, Normal Summoned Manju to search Benten, and used Hymn of Light, Tributing Benten, to Ritual Summon Saffira. Benten then searched Honest, which left both Ritual Spells in the GY as protection. It held back from a second Ritual Summon into Maxx "C", and in the End Phase it drew 2 and discarded the spare Ghost Ogre. On the opponent's turn it used Ghost Ogre to destroy Time Thief Redoer, which cleared their only monster, then used Saffira's End Phase effect to add Ghost Ogre back to hand. On turn 3 it searched Idaten with Manju and used SDQ's GY effect to Ritual Summon Sauravis, Tributing Idaten and the Manju in hand. With Idaten's boost it had 9900 damage on board. Crackdown stole a Manju, but Honest on Sauravis's attack into it made up the difference, and the player won on turn 3. I found no decisions that I could verify as mistakes.

review.summary: Going first, the player made Saffira on turn 1 with SDQ, Manju and Benten. Ghost Ogre then killed the opponent's first Redoer, and on turn 3 Sauravis negated Crackdown so both Manjus could become a second Saffira (3900 damage dealt that turn). Hymn of Light in the GY saved a Saffira from Raigeki. On turn 5 both Saffiras attacked and the opponent dropped to 2200, and Change of Heart on the lone blocker finished the game on turn 7. The main error came on turn 5. The player decided Change of Heart couldn't win because "a monster taken this turn can't attack". That ruling is wrong: Change of Heart has no attack restriction. Baiting the revealed Retrograde with the Set Forbidden Lance (Retrograde is once per turn) and then taking Redoer gave three attackers against 4100 LP, likely lethal two turns earlier. Elsewhere the player made only small value slips.

mistakes.what: Went straight to the Battle Phase and held Change of Heart, because it believed a monster taken with Change of Heart can't attack that turn. The opponent was at 4100 with Redoer (2400) and Chronocorder (1000).
mistakes.better: Change of Heart has no attack restriction. Activate the Set Forbidden Lance first to draw out the revealed Time Thief Retrograde, which works only once per turn and only while they control a Time Thief Xyz. Then Change of Heart takes Redoer. Attacks: Saffira 2500 + Saffira 2500 + Redoer 2400. Any two of the three deal at least 4900, even if Chronocorder reflects one attack, and if Chronocorder stays to block, the line does 6400. That is lethal against 4100. Even without lethal, stealing Redoer and swinging was better than holding the card.
mistakes.evidence: Change of Heart can't win this turn: a monster taken this turn can't attack

mistakes.what: Used Saffira's End Phase effect to draw 2 and then discarded Cyber Angel Idaten. It did not take back Ghost Ogre, its hand trap that had just been used against this matchup.
mistakes.better: Lesson 4 says to add a matchup-relevant hand trap back from the GY (Ghost Ogre had just answered Redoer). At minimum, discard a card with less value than the Idaten fodder.
mistakes.evidence: I'm discarding Cyber Angel Idaten, the least useful card in hand

review.summary: The player went first with Sudri, Sharnga, Gofu, Dark Armed Dragon and Delta Crow. Sudri searched Vata, and Vata sent itself plus Kris and Chinook from the Deck to summon Black-Winged Dragon. That left exactly 3 DARKs in the GY, so Dark Armed Dragon came out at the right moment. Sharnga then went into Boreastorm (set to Lv2), which made Full Armor Master, and Assault Dragon followed. On turn 2, Assault Dragon burned the opponent for 2100 and Sharnga's once-per-duel GY effect destroyed Alternative White Dragon before its destroy effect could resolve. On turn 3, Full Armor Master targeted Dragon Spirit of White and got the Tribute-for-Blue-Eyes response (more burn). Dark Armed Dragon destroyed the Blue-Eyes, and direct attacks won. I checked every decision against its listed options and found no mistakes worth counting. Gofu, Sudri's token and the Set Delta Crow (banished by Dragon Spirit) went unused, but none of them had a clearly better use.

The opponent opened with Maxx "C", but the player built Full Armor Master + Black-Winged Assault Dragon on turn 1 anyway: Sudri → Vata → BWD → Sharnga → Boreastorm → FAM → Assault. On turn 2 the player used Sharnga's GY effect to destroy Time Thief Redoer, and fired Delta Crow in the opponent's End Phase, which cleared all five Set cards (Crackdown, Solemn Warning, Solemn Strike and two Time Thief traps). Turn 3 swung for 6200 into an empty board, leaving the opponent at 400. On turn 4, Assault Dragon's 700 burn off Time Thief Winder's search ended the game. The one real error came on turn 1. Dark Armed Dragon was summonable while exactly 3 DARKs sat in the GY, but the player held it 'for later'. The Synchro line then pushed the GY past 3 DARKs and the card was dead for the rest of the game. It would have added 2800 damage on turn 3, enough to win a turn earlier.

mistakes.what: Passed on Special Summoning Dark Armed Dragon at #14 and again at #17, while the GY held exactly 3 DARK monsters (Vata, Kris, Chinook). The player kept it 'for later', but the Synchros that followed sent Sudri, Sharnga and Harmattan to the GY. That left 6 DARKs there, so DAD could never be summoned again and stayed dead in hand.
mistakes.better: Summon DAD before Synchroing. There was a free zone (Sudri M1, BWD M2, Sharnga M3), and it costs one more Maxx C draw. DAD gives a 2800 attacker plus repeatable destruction by banishing DARKs from the GY. On turn 3 that means 3200 + 3000 + 2800 = 9000 against 6600 LP, which is lethal, and its destruction effect would also have answered the opponent's turn-2 plays.
mistakes.evidence: `[2]` Special Summon "Dark Armed Dragon" from your hand ... Plan: ... Set Delta Crow. Keep DAD and Gofu.

review.summary: The player went first with Gofu, Sudri, Sharnga, Dark Armed Dragon and Delta Crow. They got Black-Winged Dragon through Sudri → Vata and added Dark Armed Dragon, then stopped. Sharnga and the Boreastorm → Full Armor Master → Assault Dragon extension were still available, and they used neither. On turn 2 Blue-Eyes destroyed BWD, removed the Set Delta Crow, beat over Dark Armed Dragon and built Titanic Galaxy, Spirit Dragon and Blue-Eyes White Dragon, with no Assault Dragon on the field to burn or wipe. On turn 3 the player made Assault Dragon but never used Sharnga's once-per-duel destroy, and summoning Assault Dragon turned it off. On turn 4 they wiped while Azure-Eyes still protected its Dragons, so only the two Spirit Dragons died. Their own board was then empty, and Titanic Galaxy, Azure-Eyes and Dragon Spirit of White dealt lethal on turn 6.

mistakes.what: With Sharnga in hand and Black-Winged Dragon (2800) on the field, the player set Delta Crow and ended the turn. Sharnga stayed in hand and the Synchro extension went unused.
mistakes.better: Special Summon Sharnga (it was offered at #21 and #23 because a 2000+ ATK monster was out). Then Synchro Summon Boreastorm with Sharnga (Lv2 Tuner) + Sudri (Lv4) and send Harmattan or Chinook so it becomes Lv2. Boreastorm (Lv2 Blackwing Tuner) + BWD (Lv8) makes Full Armor Master, and banishing Boreastorm + BWD from the GY makes Black-Winged Assault Dragon. That board is FAM + Assault + Dark Armed Dragon. FAM is unaffected by Alternative White Dragon, and Assault would have burned each monster effect on turn 2 (Alternative, both White Stones and more) and reached a wipe. Instead BWD was destroyed for free and the opponent's whole turn-2 combo went through.
mistakes.evidence: The board is already strong: Black-Winged Dragon and Dark Armed Dragon, both 2800 ATK. I'll Set Delta Crow and keep Sharnga in hand.

mistakes.what: The player passed on Sharnga's once-per-duel GY destroy at #37, #39 and #40 while Boreastorm was on the field, then banished Boreastorm for Assault Dragon. Assault Dragon is not a 'Blackwing' Synchro, so Sharnga's effect could no longer be used.
mistakes.better: Before summoning Assault Dragon, banish Sharnga to destroy Number 38 Titanic Galaxy (Sharnga is a monster effect, which its Spell negation can't stop). Titanic Galaxy later negated Enemy Controller and dealt the final 3000. The 'save it' reason didn't hold, because the next summon removed the Blackwing Synchro the effect needs.

Blue-Eyes answered with a huge Special Summon turn: a 3000-ATK Blue-Eyes, Number 38 and two Spirit Dragons. Sauravis saved Saffira and came back in the End Phase. The turning point was turn 3. The player had Honest in hand and passed without a Battle Phase, wrongly reasoning that Saffira would lose to the 3000-ATK monsters. Honest would have made the attack a 5500-ATK win, dealing 2500 damage, and Saffira's End Phase would have returned Honest. mistakes.what: Ended turn 3 without attacking, saying Saffira would lose to the 3000-ATK Blue-Eyes and Number 38, even though Honest was in hand and 'Go to the Battle Phase' was an option.
mistakes.better: Attack with Saffira and send Honest from hand in the Damage Step. She becomes 5500 against a 3000-ATK monster. If Number 38 redirects the attack, it is also 3000, so either way she destroys a boss and deals 2500 damage (6000 to 3500). Nothing on their field could stop it: Number 38 negates only Spells, and Spirit Dragon negates only GY effects. Honest going from hand to GY would also turn on Saffira's End Phase effect, which gets Honest back. That is a 3000-ATK monster and 2500 LP for free, a turn earlier.

review.summary: The player opened with a weak hand into Maxx "C". It played light: Sudri searched Shamal, Shamal placed Black Feather Whirlwind, and Delta Crow was Set. On turn 2 Delta Crow destroyed both of the opponent's Set cards (Crackdown and Retrograde), which was a strong play. On turn 3 the player sent the second Shamal to reach exactly 3 DARKs in the GY, Special Summoned Dark Armed Dragon and wiped the board, dealing 3300. The opponent fought back with Time Thief Redoer: it shuffled Dark Armed Dragon into the Deck and attached the player's top cards as material. Gofu's tokens then held off one more attack. On turn 7 the player played through Ash Blossom: it used Sudri's token to fill the GY again, Special Summoned Dark Armed Dragon, made Nothung (800 burn), revived a Blackwing with Black Feather Whirlwind, destroyed Performage Trick Clown twice and won with direct attacks. The only clear inefficiency was leaving Sharnga in Attack Position for a 500-point hit, which cost 1900 LP the next turn. That never put the win at risk.

mistakes.what: Special Summoned Sharnga in face-up Attack Position to add a 500-damage direct attack. Time Thief Redoer was banished only until the End Phase and was sure to come back.
mistakes.better: Summon Sharnga in Defense Position, or keep it in hand as a Tuner and for its later GY destroy effect. The 500 damage wasn't close to lethal (the opponent was at 4700 after the attacks), and leaving a 500 ATK body in Attack Position against a returning 2400 attacker cost 1900 LP. That brought the player down to 1700, and later to 1000.
mistakes.evidence: Redoer (ATK 2400) attacks Sharnga (face-up Attack, ATK 500) — You take 1900 damage (LP now 3300).

review.summary: The player went first through Maxx "C" and still set up Saffira on turn 1. It used Hymn of Light, Tributed Sauravis, then got Sauravis back at the End Phase, and used Manju to search Benten. Ghost Ogre destroyed the opponent's Time Thief Redoer twice, and Saffira's End Phase effect returned Ghost Ogre to hand. Sauravis negated Crackdown. Direct attacks brought the opponent to 1600 on turn 5, and Solemn Judgment's cost dropped them to 800. On turn 7 the player discarded SDQ for a second Saffira and summoned her with Hymn, Tributing Benten (which searched Honest). Saffira plus Honest then finished the game. The one real slip was on turn 5. The player never used SDQ's GY effect or its Normal Summon. Summoning Sauravis (Tributing Benten and Manju, Benten searching Honest) and then Normal Summoning Honest gave enough attackers to win through Chronocorder's damage redirect.

mistakes.what: Went straight to the Battle Phase with only Saffira and Manju against 4100 LP. It left the SDQ GY Ritual Summon unused (it was option [0]), along with its Normal Summon, while holding Sauravis and Benten.
mistakes.better: Banish SDQ from the GY to Ritual Summon Sauravis (Lv7, 2600 ATK), Tributing Benten from hand plus Manju (6+4). Benten's Tribute effect searches Honest, and the Normal Summon puts Honest on the field. That gives three attackers: 2500 + 2600 + 1100 = 6200. Chronocorder redirects only one hit, so attack with Honest first: 5100 damage against 4100 LP is lethal. The set Solemn Judgment could have negated the summon, but that card was unknown. The line also spent nothing that mattered, since Benten replaces itself.

review.summary: The player went first with Sudri, Sharnga, Gofu, Dark Armed Dragon and Delta Crow. On turn 1 they thought Vata's effect wasn't offered, though it was, and turned the whole combo into Nothung and then a lone Black-Winged Dragon, when they could have had BWD plus Boreastorm and then Full Armor Master or Assault Dragon. Solemn Judgment and Crackdown took apart that thin board on turn 3. After that, three misreads and a careless position choice cost the player life points and cards. They turned down Gofu's two tokens thinking the prompt was its banish effect. They Normal Summoned Vayu in Attack Position instead of Setting it and took 1600 damage. On turn 7 they turned down Sudri's free search, thinking the prompt was its Tribute effect. The opponent's Raigeki plus a 1600 direct attack finished them from exactly 1600 LP. Either the tokens (which would have blocked the 1800 Winder hit) or the Set Vayu (which would have avoided the 1600) alone would probably have kept the player alive.

mistakes.what: The player wrote that Vata's effect wasn't offered, even though option [1] was Vata's field effect (the engine labelled it "Special Summon this card"; the script's only on-field effect is the send-to-GY → BWD). They Synchro Summoned Nothung with Vata + Sudri, then made BWD out of Nothung + Sharnga and ended with one monster.
mistakes.better: Use Vata (sending Vata + Simoon from the Deck) → BWD, keeping Sudri. Then Special Summon Sharnga (BWD is 2800 ATK on the field), Synchro Summon Boreastorm (Sharnga + Sudri), set it to Lv2, and make Full Armor Master (Boreastorm + BWD) or Assault Dragon. That is a far stronger first-turn board than a lone BWD for Crackdown to steal.
